title: LDR raw ADC polarity is circuit-dependent
symptoms: Generated light threshold logic is inverted.
Code assumes raw ADC increases with brightness without calibration evidence.
GL5516/GraftSense light projects compare raw ADC values directly.
wrong_pattern: Treating raw ADC > threshold as brighter light, or raw ADC < threshold as darker light, without naming and validating the divider polarity.
correct_pattern: Prefer calibrated driver APIs such as set_min_light(), set_max_light(), and get_calibrated_light(). If raw ADC thresholds are unavoidable, put the polarity assumption in conf.py and generated logs/comments, for example RAW_ADC_DECREASES_WITH_LIGHT = True, and ask the user to calibrate or confirm the divider direction.
fix_guidance: For GraftSense GL5516, treat the README statement as concrete evidence: stronger light gives a smaller ADC value.
Use calibration APIs when the selected driver exposes them: set_min_light(), set_max_light(), and get_calibrated_light().
Do not generate naked raw ADC comparisons unless the polarity is explicitly represented in configuration and user-facing logs.
When the divider circuit is unknown, require calibration or user confirmation before claiming a bright/dark threshold is correct.
Name threshold constants by calibrated meaning, such as LIGHT_PERCENT_THRESHOLD, instead of ambiguous raw ADC names when using calibrated values.

references.label: GraftSense GL5516 README
references.evidence: The README states that as light intensity increases, ADC value decreases, and documents set_min_light(), set_max_light(), and get_calibrated_light().

references.label: GraftSense GL5516 driver context
references.evidence: Driver context exposes GL5516 calibration and calibrated light APIs.

verified_by: Generated code uses calibrated light percentage APIs when available.
Any raw ADC threshold declares its polarity assumption in conf.py.
Generated logs or README text ask for calibration when the divider direction is unknown.
